title: Signals Collector Technician (Sig Coll Tech)
raw_text:
8-352S. MOS 352S--Signals Collector Technician (Sig Coll Tech) (Effective 202211)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21.
   c. MOS 352S. MOS 352S is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 35S. All 352S
MOS holders must be graduates of either A-231-0451 (Intermediate Communications Signals
Analysis Course) or SIGE3810 (Intermediate Technical Electronic Intelligence Analysis Course),
or have completed the Military Cryptologic Signals Analysis Program (MCSAP).
   d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS).
       (1) Q1--Interactive On-Net Operator (Personnel Only).
       (2) Q2--Target Digital Network Analyst (Personnel Only)
       (3) Q3--Cryptologic Cyber Analyst (Personnel Only).
       (4) V3--Aerial Precision Geo-Location (APG). (Rescind 202204)
   f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
               (b) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI).
               (c) Soldiers are required to receive and pass a counterintelligence scope polygraph
(CSP) prior to being awarded the MOS and must continue to pass subsequent CSPs to hold the
MOS. Soldiers who refuse to take or fail a CSP are no longer qualified in their primary MOS.
               (d) Soldiers must be eligible to gain system and/or facility access controlled by the
NSA. Soldiers who are not granted NSA system and/or facility access after 12 months of access
request date will lose qualification in their primary MOS (PMOS). Commanders will initiate
reclassification or separation actions for the Soldier. The access request date is defined as the
date that the NSA receives a completed Security In-processing Packet. This process begins after
the Soldier has received a fully adjudicated TS/SCI clearance and has completed the required
CSP.
               (e) Complete the Signals Collector Technician MI Warrant Officer Basic Course
(WOBC).
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the resident MI Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE)
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
   g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2 --
               (a) Manages personnel and equipment to collect, process, locate, identify, analyze
and report on SIGINT information to support tactical, operational, and strategic requirements
across all domains
               (b) Manages training for subordinates and peers on technical, operational, and
tactical SIGINT skills required to perform the mission
               (c) Coordinates staff actions to fulfill all requirements in support of SIGINT mission
activities and the Commander’s intent.
               (d) Advises the commander and staff with regard to SIGINT operations, activities,
and personnel.
               (e) May serve as a Discipline Analyst or Functional Manager at any echelon.
        (2) CW3 --
              (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Provides technical guidance and direction to subordinate intelligence elements.
              (c) Utilizes of signals intelligence collection personnel and equipment by the
allocations of all non-Morse resources.
              (d) Manages non-Morse related SIGINT systems to ensure cost and technically
effective life-cycle training support is planned and provided for these systems.
              (e) May serve as a Discipline Collection Manager at any echelon.
              (f) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
              (g) May serve as a Detachment Commander.
              (h) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
              (i) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
              (j) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
        (3) CW4--
              (a) Manages, directs and performs duties shown in paragraph g(1) and g(2).
              (b) Provides technical guidance and direction to subordinate intelligence elements. .
              (c) Utilizes signals intelligence collection personnel and equipment to conduct the
allocations of all non-Morse resources.
              (d) Manages non-Morse related SIGINT systems to ensure cost and technically
effective life-cycle training support is planned and provided for these systems.
              (e) May serve as a Discipline Collection Manager at any echelon.
              (f) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
              (g) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
              (h) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
              (i) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
              (j) May serve as the HRC MI WO Assignments Manager.
        (4) CW5 --
              (a) MI CW5s are proficient in the duties described in the duties paragraphs of one or
more MI WO MOSs.
              (b) MI CW5s are branch technical experts and master-level technical and tactical
experts who perform the primary duties of technical leader, manager, multidiscipline intelligence
integrator, and advisor.
              (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
              (d) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship,
advice, and counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers and have special
warrant officer leadership and representation responsibilities within their respective commands
              (e) Primarily support division, corps, echelons above corps, and major command
operations.
              (f) Advise commanders and branch assignment managers on the assignments and
placement of Military Intelligence warrant officers world-wide.
              (g) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform
other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities.
              (h) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
              (i) May serve on the Army Staff.
              (j) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief.
              (k) May serve as the MI WO Proponent.
              (l) May serve as the CCWO of the MI Branch.
              (m) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have competed the WO Senior
Service Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets..
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
        (2) A physical profile of 222211.
          (3) Have normal color discrimination with corrected vision per one of the following three
categories of the good eye, bad eye categories: 20/40-20/70; 20/30-20/100; or, 20/20/400,
         (4) Have hearing wherein sound amplitude in one ear does not exceed 45 decibels at
frequencies 250, 500, 1000, and 2000 CPS (HZ) or 65 decibels at frequency 4000.
         (5) Qualifying Scores
         A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 350
cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs, and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 36 shuttles in Physical
Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (6) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-352S-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-352S-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
